laws.rule: Hannover charges an accommodation tax per adult guest per night by price band: nothing up to EUR 25, EUR 3 up to EUR 50, EUR 4 up to EUR 100 (about A$6.36, RBA rate of 30 October 2026), then EUR 1 more for each further EUR 50 or part, capped at EUR 12; breakfast and parking are not counted.

laws.rule: The Harz National Park also covers the western Harz (around Bad Harzburg, Torfhaus and Sankt Andreasberg) in Lower Saxony. The same park rules apply there as in Saxony-Anhalt: paths only, dogs on a lead, no open fire or smoking, no camping, no drones. The full wording is held on the Saxony-Anhalt page.
laws.heading: Nationalpark Harz, Verhaltensregeln im Nationalpark Harz

laws.rule: Lower Saxony Wadden Sea National Park (Zone 1 / Ruhezone, about 68.5% of the park; Zone 2 / Zwischenzone, about 31%; Zone 3 / Erholungszone, about 0.5%): Zone 1 may be entered all year only on approved, marked paths. Zone 2 may be entered freely, except from 1 April to 31 July (breeding and rearing season) when only the paths may be used. Zone 3 is mostly bathing beaches where holiday activities such as swimming, sunbathing, fishing and shell collecting are allowed, but camping tents and caravans, noisy events and motorised leisure vehicles such as beach buggies are not. In Zones 1 and 2, dogs may be walked on a lead only, and visiting, photographing or filming animals at their breeding and rearing sites is not allowed. Local councils set their own rules, especially for dog beaches and kite areas.

laws.rule: Lower Saxony Wadden Sea National Park, Zones 1 and 2: flying kites, drones or model aircraft is not allowed, and kitesurfing and buggy-kiting are prohibited except in areas the park approves. The park tells visitors to check local rules for the beach zone.

laws.rule: Lower Saxony's holiday law protects Sundays and public holidays from 7 am to 11 am: public open-air meetings and parades that are not tied to worship, entertainment or pleasure events that do not serve a higher interest of art, science or public education, and events or acts that disturb a religious or philosophical ceremony or make it harder to reach one, are banned in those hours, except on 1 May and 3 October (section 5). On Good Friday, events in rooms with bar service that go beyond serving food and drink, public sport events, and other public events are also banned, unless the other public events serve spiritual uplift or a higher interest of art, science or public education and respect the serious character of the day (section 6(1)). On Volkstrauertag and Totensonntag those extra bar-service bans run from 5 am, commercial public sport events are banned, non-commercial public sport events are banned if they include parades, entertainment music or festival events, and other public events face the same exception as on Good Friday (section 6(2)). Public dance events are banned from 5 am on Maundy Thursday, on Holy Saturday, and on Christmas Eve (section 9). A breach can be fined (section 13; the statute does not set a maximum amount).
